title: Psalms Chapter 112 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 112 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 112 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 112.

questions.question: According to Psalms 112:1, who is blessed?
options: The man that feareth the LORD and delighteth greatly in his commandments
The man who has great wealth
The man who is mighty upon earth
The man who is righteous forever
questions.correctAnswer: The man that feareth the LORD and delighteth greatly in his commandments
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:1 states that blessed is the man that feareth the LORD and delighteth greatly in his commandments.

questions.question: What is said about the seed of the upright in Psalms 112:2?
options: His seed shall be mighty upon earth
His seed shall be few and humble
His seed shall wander in the desert
His seed shall not be remembered
questions.correctAnswer: His seed shall be mighty upon earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:2 says that his seed shall be mighty upon earth, indicating strength and blessing for the generation of the upright.

questions.question: What shall be in the house of the man who is righteous according to Psalms 112:3?
options: Wealth and riches
Only humble possessions
Peace and quiet
Enemies and troubles
questions.correctAnswer: Wealth and riches
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:3 states that wealth and riches shall be in his house, and his righteousness endureth forever.

questions.question: According to Psalms 112:4, what arises unto the upright?
options: Light in the darkness
Storms and trials
Enemies and fear
Silence and rest
questions.correctAnswer: Light in the darkness
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:4 says unto the upright there ariseth light in the darkness, indicating hope and guidance.

questions.question: Which traits are attributed to the upright person in Psalms 112:4?
options: Gracious, full of compassion, and righteous
Proud, unforgiving, and harsh
Silent, fearful, and weak
Greedy, selfish, and proud
questions.correctAnswer: Gracious, full of compassion, and righteous
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:4 describes the upright as gracious, full of compassion, and righteous.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 112:5 says a good man will lend and show favor.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:5 states that a good man sheweth favour, and lendeth, showing kindness and generosity.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 112:6, the righteous shall be moved forever.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:6 says surely he shall not be moved forever, indicating the stability of the righteous.

questions.question: What does Psalms 112:7 say about the heart of the righteous?
options: His heart is fixed, trusting in the LORD
His heart is afraid of evil tidings
His heart is weak and doubtful
His heart desires riches
questions.correctAnswer: His heart is fixed, trusting in the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:7 states that he shall not be afraid of evil tidings; his heart is fixed, trusting in the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 112:8 says the righteous will be afraid until they see their desire upon their enemies.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:8 states his heart is established, he shall not be afraid, until he see his desire upon his enemies, meaning he remains confident and unafraid.

questions.question: According to Psalms 112:9, what has the righteous man done?
options: He hath dispersed and given to the poor
He hath gathered wealth for himself
He hath hidden his blessings
He hath ignored the needy
questions.correctAnswer: He hath dispersed and given to the poor
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:9 states he hath dispersed, he hath given to the poor, highlighting generosity.

questions.question: What will happen to the wicked according to Psalms 112:10?
options: They shall be grieved, gnash with teeth, and melt away
They shall prosper and be honored
They shall be protected by the LORD
They shall be forgotten immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be grieved, gnash with teeth, and melt away
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:10 describes the wicked seeing it and being grieved, gnashing with their teeth, and melting away.

questions.question: In Psalms 112, which comes first?
options: The man who feareth the LORD is blessed
The wicked shall gnash with their teeth
The righteous will not be moved forever
The righteous shall give to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: The man who feareth the LORD is blessed
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:1 comes before the other events and states that the man who feareth the LORD is blessed.

questions.question: What is said about the generation of the upright in Psalms 112:2?
options: It shall be blessed
It shall be cursed
It shall be forgotten
It shall be weak
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be blessed
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:2 says the generation of the upright shall be blessed.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 112:3 says that the righteousness of the upright will last forever.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:3 states his righteousness endureth forever.

questions.question: According to Psalms 112:5, how does a good man guide his affairs?
options: With discretion
With haste
With selfishness
Without care
questions.correctAnswer: With discretion
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:5 states a good man will guide his affairs with discretion.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 112 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 112 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 112:5, how does a good man manage his affairs?
options: With rash decisions and impatience
With discretion and lending with favour
By seeking personal gain only
By avoiding all risks
questions.correctAnswer: With discretion and lending with favour
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:5 states that a good man shows favour and lends, guiding his affairs with discretion, highlighting generosity and wise management.

questions.question: What assurance does Psalms 112:6 give to the righteous person?
options: They will be wealthy for a short time
They shall not be moved forever and will be remembered
They will face constant hardship
Their enemies will rule over them
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not be moved forever and will be remembered
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:6 promises that the righteous will not be moved forever and will be in everlasting remembrance, showing stability and lasting honor.

questions.question: How does Psalms 112:7 describe the heart of the person who trusts in the LORD?
options: Fearful and anxious about evil tidings
Fixed and not afraid of evil tidings
Doubtful and wavering
Unconcerned and indifferent
questions.correctAnswer: Fixed and not afraid of evil tidings
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:7 explains that the person who trusts in the LORD has a fixed heart and will not fear evil tidings, illustrating confident faith.

questions.question: What is the relationship between trust in God and fear of enemies as outlined in Psalms 112:8?
options: Trust causes fear to increase
Trust establishes the heart so fear is removed until desires are seen upon enemies
Fear is irrelevant regardless of trust
Trust leads to ignoring enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Trust establishes the heart so fear is removed until desires are seen upon enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:8 shows that with trust, the heart is established and fear is removed until one sees their desire upon enemies, linking faith with courage and hope.

questions.question: What does Psalms 112:5 teach about generosity and wisdom in practical living?
options: A good person should avoid lending to others
Showing favour and lending with discretion is wise and generous
Generosity is not important
Wisdom is shown by keeping wealth to oneself
questions.correctAnswer: Showing favour and lending with discretion is wise and generous
questions.explanation: Verse 5 teaches that generosity combined with discretion in lending shows practical wisdom and kindness in daily life.

questions.question: What promise in Psalms 112:6 can encourage someone facing instability or trials?
options: They will be temporarily unsettled but finally moved
The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance and not be moved forever
Their troubles will last forever
Their name will be forgotten
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance and not be moved forever
questions.explanation: This verse provides assurance that the righteous have lasting stability and remembrance despite trials, offering hope and encouragement.

questions.question: In Psalms 112:7, what is the source of the fixed heart that is not afraid of evil tidings?
options: Trust in human strength
Trust in the LORD
Ignoring problems
Avoiding all news
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the heart is fixed and not afraid because it trusts in the LORD, emphasizing reliance on God for courage.

questions.question: How does Psalms 112:8 describe the emotional state of a person established in their heart?
options: Fearful until enemies are defeated
Unafraid until they see their desire upon their enemies
Anxious and doubtful
Indifferent to their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Unafraid until they see their desire upon their enemies
questions.explanation: The verse teaches that the person’s heart is established and they are not afraid until they witness their desire fulfilled over their enemies, showing confidence and patience.

questions.question: What does Psalms 112:6 imply will happen if a person follows the instruction in Psalms 112:5 to guide affairs with discretion?
options: They will be easily moved and forgotten
They shall not be moved forever and will be remembered
They will face constant fear
Their wealth will quickly vanish
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not be moved forever and will be remembered
questions.explanation: Verse 6 promises stability and everlasting remembrance for the righteous, implying that discretion in managing affairs (verse 5) leads to enduring honor and strength.

questions.question: What does Psalms 112:8 promise will happen if the heart is fixed and trusting in the LORD as described in Psalms 112:7?
options: The person will fear their enemies
Their heart will be established and they will not be afraid until they see their desire upon enemies
They will be moved by evil tidings
They will lose their trust
questions.correctAnswer: Their heart will be established and they will not be afraid until they see their desire upon enemies
questions.explanation: Building on verse 7’s trust, verse 8 promises that the heart is then firmly established without fear until desires are realized over enemies, demonstrating growth in faith and courage.

questions.question: How does Psalms 112:5–7 collectively teach about the virtue of faith during adversity?
options: Faith removes the need to manage affairs wisely
Faith causes fear of evil tidings
Faith leads to discretion, favour, and a fixed heart not fearing evil tidings
Faith prevents generosity
questions.correctAnswer: Faith leads to discretion, favour, and a fixed heart not fearing evil tidings
questions.explanation: Verses 5 through 7 connect generosity and wise management with a heart fixed in trust that removes fear, teaching how faith sustains wise and compassionate living during trials.

questions.question: A fellow believer is anxious about bad news concerning their personal struggles. According to Psalms 112:7, what biblical truth can you share to encourage them?
options: They should ignore the news because it's unimportant
They should fear the news as it will bring harm
They can fix their heart and not be afraid by trusting in the LORD
They must rely on their own strength only
questions.correctAnswer: They can fix their heart and not be afraid by trusting in the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:7 teaches that trusting in the LORD fixes the heart and removes fear of evil tidings, providing comfort and courage in anxious times.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 112:6, the righteous will eventually be forgotten over time.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:6 states the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance and shall not be moved forever, meaning they will not be forgotten.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 112:8 indicates that a person’s heart will remain afraid until they completely avoid their enemies.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 112:8 says the heart shall not be afraid until the person sees their desire upon their enemies, not that fear continues while avoiding them.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 112:5 suggests that a good man shows favour and lends, guiding his affairs with discretion.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that a good man shows favour and lends, managing his affairs with discretion, highlighting generosity and wise leadership.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 112 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 112.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'his horn shall be exalted with honour' in Psalms 112:9 symbolize?
options: His power and strength
His wealth and riches
His wisdom and knowledge
His humility
questions.correctAnswer: His power and strength
questions.explanation: The phrase 'his horn shall be exalted with honour' uses 'horn' as a symbol of power and strength, as indicated in Psalms 112:9. This imagery is consistent with other biblical uses of 'horn' as a symbol of strength, such as in 1 Samuel 2:1.

questions.question: According to Psalms 112:10, what is the reaction of the wicked when they see the blessings of the righteous?
options: They rejoice and praise God
They are grieved and gnash their teeth
They ignore and turn away
They seek to imitate the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: They are grieved and gnash their teeth
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:10 states that 'The wicked shall see it, and be grieved; he shall gnash with his teeth, and melt away.' This shows the wicked's negative reaction to the prosperity of the righteous.

questions.question: Psalms 112:9 describes the righteous as having given to the poor. Which New Testament teaching echoes this theme of generosity?
options: Matthew 25:40 - Whatever you did for one of the least of these
John 3:16 - God so loved the world
Romans 8:28 - All things work together for good
Hebrews 11:1 - Faith is the substance of things hoped for
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 25:40 - Whatever you did for one of the least of these
questions.explanation: The generosity described in Psalms 112:9 is echoed in Matthew 25:40, where Jesus teaches that acts of kindness to the poor are acts done unto Him.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'his righteousness endureth for ever' in Psalms 112:9 imply about the nature of the righteous man's actions?
options: His righteousness is temporary and fleeting
His righteousness is lasting and continual
His righteousness is only for this life
His righteousness is hidden and secret
questions.correctAnswer: His righteousness is lasting and continual
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:9 states that 'his righteousness endureth for ever,' indicating that the righteousness of the man is permanent and lasting beyond his earthly life.

questions.question: In Psalms 112:7, what is the basis for the righteous man's fearlessness in the face of evil tidings?
options: His wealth and riches
His trust in the LORD
His military strength
His wisdom and knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: His trust in the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:7 says, 'his heart is fixed, trusting in the LORD,' showing that the righteous man's confidence and lack of fear stem from his trust in God.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in Psalms 112:4 when contrasting 'light in the darkness' with the upright man?
options: Simile
Metaphor
Chiasm
Parallelism
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:4 uses the metaphor of 'light in the darkness' to describe the upright man's positive qualities, symbolizing guidance and hope amidst adversity.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 112:6, the righteous man will be in everlasting remembrance.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:6 explicitly states, 'the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance,' affirming the lasting legacy of the righteous.

questions.question: In Psalms 112:5, a good man is described as one who 'lendeth.' What does this indicate about his character in the cultural context of the ancient Near East?
options: He is selfish and hoards wealth
He is generous and trustworthy
He is a moneylender who profits from others
He is indifferent to others’ needs
questions.correctAnswer: He is generous and trustworthy
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, lending was an act of generosity and benevolence. Psalms 112:5 indicates that a good man is one who shows favor and lends, reflecting generosity and discretion.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word likely underlies the phrase 'full of compassion' in Psalms 112:4, and what is its significance?
options: Chesed - lovingkindness or steadfast love
Ruach - spirit or breath
Shema - to hear or obey
Melech - king
questions.correctAnswer: Chesed - lovingkindness or steadfast love
questions.explanation: 'Full of compassion' in Psalms 112:4 is often translated from the Hebrew 'chesed,' which means lovingkindness or steadfast love, emphasizing the moral character of the upright man.

questions.question: How does Psalms 112:8 illustrate the concept of patience and trust in God's justice?
options: By showing immediate vengeance on enemies
By stating the heart will not fear until the desire is fulfilled
By ignoring enemies completely
By seeking human revenge
questions.correctAnswer: By stating the heart will not fear until the desire is fulfilled
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:8 says, 'His heart is established, he shall not be afraid, until he see his desire upon his enemies,' illustrating patient trust in the eventual fulfillment of God's justice.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the wicked's gnashing of teeth found in Psalms 112:10?
options: Revelation 20:15 - The lake of fire
Matthew 8:12 - Where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
John 11:35 - Jesus wept
Acts 2:38 - Repent and be baptized
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 8:12 - Where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:12 uses the phrase 'weeping and gnashing of teeth' to describe the fate of the wicked, echoing the imagery in Psalms 112:10.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'he hath dispersed' in Psalms 112:9 in terms of ancient Near Eastern social ethics?
options: It reflects selfish accumulation of wealth
It indicates an act of social responsibility and generosity
It means he scattered his enemies
It implies careless spending
questions.correctAnswer: It indicates an act of social responsibility and generosity
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, 'dispersion' of wealth by the righteous, as in Psalms 112:9, signified generosity and care for the poor, highlighting social ethics of justice.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 112:3 suggests that the righteousness of the upright man is temporary and will fade with time.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:3 says, 'his righteousness endureth for ever,' directly contradicting the idea of temporariness and affirming the everlasting nature of the upright man's righteousness.

questions.question: Which earlier Scripture theme does Psalms 112:1, about fearing the LORD and delighting in His commandments, develop and fulfill?
options: The Decalogue's call to obedience (Exodus 20)
The creation account in Genesis 1
The Exodus from Egypt
The building of the Temple
questions.correctAnswer: The Decalogue's call to obedience (Exodus 20)
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:1 emphasizes fearing the LORD and delighting in His commandments, developing the obedience theme first given in the Ten Commandments in Exodus 20.

questions.question: How does Psalms 112:2 use parallelism to emphasize the blessing upon the upright man's descendants?
options: By repeating the same idea in two synonymous phrases
By contrasting the righteous and the wicked
By using a metaphor of light and darkness
By employing chiasmus structure
questions.correctAnswer: By repeating the same idea in two synonymous phrases
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:2 uses synonymous parallelism: 'His seed shall be mighty upon earth: the generation of the upright shall be blessed,' repeating the blessing theme to emphasize its certainty.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 112 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 112 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Psalms 112:1, what characterizes the man who is blessed?
options: He fears the LORD and delights greatly in His commandments
He is wealthy and has many children
He is wise and never makes mistakes
He always speaks truth and judges righteously
questions.correctAnswer: He fears the LORD and delights greatly in His commandments
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:1 explicitly states, 'Blessed is the man that feareth the LORD, that delighteth greatly in his commandments,' showing that the fear of God combined with delight in His law marks the blessed man.

questions.question: What does Psalms 112:2 teach about the descendants of the upright?
options: Their seed shall be mighty upon earth
Their descendants will be poor and oppressed
Their lineage will be cut off
Their children will be unknown
questions.correctAnswer: Their seed shall be mighty upon earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:2 promises that 'His seed shall be mighty upon earth: the generation of the upright shall be blessed,' indicating God's blessing extends to the righteous man's posterity.

questions.question: What eternal quality does Psalms 112:3 attribute to the righteousness of the blessed man?
options: His righteousness endureth forever
His righteousness is temporary
His righteousness depends on wealth
His righteousness is hidden
questions.correctAnswer: His righteousness endureth forever
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 112:3, 'his righteousness endureth for ever,' emphasizing the everlasting nature of the upright man's righteousness.

questions.question: Which attributes are ascribed to the upright man in Psalms 112:4?
options: Gracious, full of compassion, and righteous
Proud, judgmental, and harsh
Silent, fearful, and weak
Wise, wealthy, and powerful
questions.correctAnswer: Gracious, full of compassion, and righteous
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:4 describes the upright as one who 'is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous,' highlighting key moral virtues.

questions.question: How does Psalms 112:5 describe the conduct of a good man in managing his affairs?
options: He shews favour, lends, and guides his affairs with discretion
He hoards wealth and ignores the poor
He acts impulsively and selfishly
He trusts in his own strength alone
questions.correctAnswer: He shews favour, lends, and guides his affairs with discretion
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:5 states, 'A good man sheweth favour, and lendeth: he will guide his affairs with discretion,' indicating generosity combined with wise stewardship.

questions.question: What doctrine of eternal security is suggested by Psalms 112:6 about the righteous?
options: The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance and shall not be moved forever
The righteous will fall away and be forgotten
The righteous are only temporarily secure
The righteous depend on human memory for security
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance and shall not be moved forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:6 declares, 'Surely he shall not be moved for ever: the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance,' affirming the doctrine that God's people have eternal security and honor.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified by the man in Psalms 112:7 who trusts in the LORD and fears no evil tidings?
options: God's faithfulness and protection
God's wrath and judgment
God's hiddenness
God's silence
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness and protection
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:7 says, 'His heart is fixed, trusting in the LORD,' showing trust grounded in God's faithfulness and protective care.

questions.question: How does Psalms 112:8 illustrate the perseverance of faith in the face of opposition?
options: The heart is established and not afraid until seeing desire upon enemies
The heart is fearful and flees from enemies
Faith is abandoned when enemies prevail
The heart relies on its own strength against enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The heart is established and not afraid until seeing desire upon enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:8 states, 'His heart is established, he shall not be afraid, until he see his desire upon his enemies,' describing steadfast faith that endures opposition.

questions.question: What social doctrine is taught through the actions described in Psalms 112:9 concerning the righteous man?
options: He disperses wealth and gives to the poor, demonstrating social justice
He accumulates wealth and ignores the needy
He isolates himself from society
He only helps those who can repay him
questions.correctAnswer: He disperses wealth and gives to the poor, demonstrating social justice
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:9 says, 'He hath dispersed, he hath given to the poor; his righteousness endureth for ever,' indicating the righteous man's commitment to generosity and justice.

questions.question: What eschatological hope is expressed in Psalms 112:10 regarding the fate of the wicked?
options: The wicked shall gnash their teeth and melt away; their desire shall perish
The wicked will triumph over the righteous
The wicked will be forgotten without consequence
The wicked will be exalted and honored
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked shall gnash their teeth and melt away; their desire shall perish
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:10 predicts, 'The wicked shall see it, and be grieved; he shall gnash with his teeth, and melt away: the desire of the wicked shall perish,' pointing to final judgment and loss.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 112:3 and Psalms 112:9 convey about righteousness and generosity?
options: Righteousness endures forever and is demonstrated by giving to the poor
Righteousness is fleeting and unrelated to generosity
Generosity leads to loss of righteousness
Righteousness is only about personal piety
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness endures forever and is demonstrated by giving to the poor
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:3 notes that 'his righteousness endureth for ever,' and 112:9 shows this righteousness through generosity to the poor, linking moral virtue with social responsibility.

questions.question: How do Psalms 112:5 and Psalms 112:6 together provide insight into the doctrine of sanctification?
options: Discretion and favor in dealings lead to stability and lasting remembrance
Sanctification requires isolation from the world
Sanctification is only about internal feelings without actions
The righteous are often unstable and forgotten
questions.correctAnswer: Discretion and favor in dealings lead to stability and lasting remembrance
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows the righteous acting with favor and discretion, and verse 6 promises they 'shall not be moved for ever' and will be remembered eternally, highlighting progressive sanctification in character and legacy.

questions.question: What theological synthesis emerges from Psalms 112:1 and Psalms 112:7 about faith and fear?
options: Fear of the LORD leads to trust and freedom from fear of evil tidings
Fear of the LORD leads to constant anxiety
Trust in the LORD is irrelevant to fearing God
Fear and faith cannot coexist
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of the LORD leads to trust and freedom from fear of evil tidings
questions.explanation: Psalms 112:1 links blessing to fearing God, while 112:7 describes the trusting heart that is not afraid of evil news, showing how reverence for God results in peace and confidence.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 112:6-8 promotes a self-reliant confidence rather than trust in God. What does Psalms 112:6-8 actually teach about the source of security?
options: Security comes from a heart fixed and trusting in the LORD, not self-reliance
Security is based on human wisdom alone
Security is an illusion and not promised
Security depends on avoiding all troubles
questions.correctAnswer: Security comes from a heart fixed and trusting in the LORD, not self-reliance
questions.explanation: These verses emphasize a heart 'fixed, trusting in the LORD' (v7) and being unafraid (v8), making clear that true security is grounded in divine trust, not human strength, countering sceptical claims.

questions.question: How does Psalms 112:4 reflect the attribute of God's justice as it relates to the upright?
options: The upright are righteous and compassionate, reflecting God's justice
The upright are harsh and unforgiving
The upright ignore justice
The upright rely on human standards of fairness
questions.correctAnswer: The upright are righteous and compassionate, reflecting God's justice
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states the upright man is 'righteous' and 'full of compassion,' attributes that mirror God's just and merciful nature, showing how divine justice is lived out.
